Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-25 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Alex Mercer (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jules Kim (Redwood Solutions Eng); Priya Rao (CTO, Verdant), Marco Diaz (ML), Tara Nguyen (Infra), Ellen Park (Product)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
Quick sync to align on POC scope focused on integration mechanics — SDKs, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function calling and structured outputs, plus benchmarks to validate latency/throughput under Verdant workloads. Redwood to share security docs and spin up trial endpoints.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll do a quick intro and then dig into the integration plan — just to confirm this is a POC scoping right?
[00:12] Priya (CTO): yes, thanks Alex, we want to validate integration with our existing ML infra and ensure latency/quality tradeoffs are ok. We're trying not to change our app logic much so OpenAI compatibility is important.
[00:25] Samir (SE): got it. so two big buckets: API compatibility / SDKs and the benchmark tests — latency, throughput, p95, cost per 1k tokens. also func or tool calling if you need it.
[00:36] Marco (ML): quick background: our user journeys are mostly synchronous chat + structured extraction for downstream analytics. Typical session is ~1.8k tokens per user per day, peaks at 400 concurrent sessions during ingest windows.
[00:50] Tara (Infra): our infra is in GCP with VPC peering options; we also have strict KMS usage and require audit logs forwarded to our splunk instance.
[01:02] Alex (AE): perfect. for the POC success criteria, what would you like to measure? p95 latency target, throughput, quality threshold?
[01:12] Priya (CTO): p95 under 400ms is ideal for chat, but we can accept up to 700ms for heavy context loads. Quality: paraphrase fidelity >90% on our evaluation prompts and structured JSON extraction accuracy >95% on entity fields. Cost target is important but secondary for POC.
[01:32] Jules (Solutions Eng): noted, we'll codify those. on structured outputs, do you have a JSON schema you want the model to adhere to?
[01:39] Ellen (Product): yes, we have a lightweight schema for the extracted entities — I'll share a sample. we need deterministic structure for downstream pipelines.
[01:48] Samir (SE): cool. Redwood supports function/tool calling and structured output constraints; in practice we'll use a JSON schema validation layer and a retry fallback if the model deviates. small note: sometimes the transcriber shows "KV catch" instead of "KV cache" — apologies for typos in the transcript.
[02:05] Marco (ML): about OpenAI compatibility, our app uses the OpenAI SDK heavily. we prefer an endpoint where we can swap in Redwood with minimal changes — same params, streaming, function call hooks.
[02:17] Samir (SE): that's exactly supported. we expose an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and have official SDKs in Python and Node that mirror that behaviour. streaming and function-calling are supported; there are a couple of param name mismatches in older SDK versions but we'll give you the exact mapping.
[02:33] Priya (CTO): what about rate limits and token quotas? we run large batch jobs overnight that hit high token counts.
[02:41] Alex (AE): for the POC we'll provision a dedicated trial pool sized to your estimate; for production we can discuss Dedicated or Private (VPC) options. for trials we can increase quotas temporarily.
[02:52] Tara (Infra): if we do anything with Private, we need VPC peering or on-prem option and KMS integration. do you support HSM-backed keys?
[03:01] Samir (SE): yes KMS integrations are supported; HSM varies by customer but we have partners. audit logs and SSO/SAML are part of the enterprise add-on. we'll include the compliance pack in the follow-up.
[03:13] Ellen (Product): timeline? how long for the POC to run benchmarks and reach acceptance?
[03:18] Jules (Solutions Eng): typical POC 4-6 weeks: week 0 provisioning and integration, week 1-2 dry run + small benchmarks, week 3 full benchmark and edge case tests, week 4 acceptance and go/no-go. we can compress if you can provide dataset and schema promptly.
[03:34] Marco (ML): dataset — we'll share 48 hours of representative logs and a set of 200 evaluation prompts. those should simulate peak and tail latencies.
[03:44] Alex (AE): perfect. for sizing: you mentioned 400 concurrent sessions peak; can you translate to tokens/sec for model selection?
[03:52] Marco (ML): approx 1,200 tokens/sec sustained during peaks, bursts up to 3,000 tok/s for short periods. average session length variable, some long contexts with up to 6k context tokens.
[04:05] Samir (SE): good to know. for long contexts we may suggest a quantized model variant or a KV cache strategy to reduce repeated encoder work. Redwood runtime supports prefix caching and contin... continous batching.
[04:19] Tara (Infra): how invasive is the SDK? we want minimal changes — ideally swap endpoint URL and keep same client code.
[04:26] Samir (SE): that's how the OpenAI-compatible endpoint works — same request/response shapes, streaming chunks, function calling payloads. we'll send a migration diff.
[04:35] Priya (CTO): about function/tool calling — we rely on it to call our internal enrichment service. can Redwood proxies calls or do you recommend local orchestration?
[04:45] Jules (Solutions Eng): we recommend local orchestration for sensitive data — the model returns structured function call payloads which your service then executes. Redwood can also host tool proxies in dedicated deployments if needed, but that adds ops.
[04:58] Marco (ML): and reliability — we need graceful degradation: fallback to smaller model or cached responses when capacity is constrained.
[05:05] Alex (AE): Redwood has smart routing and automatic fallbacks to compatible variants; for POC we'll set policies to fall back to a lower-cost model when latency spikes, and we'll show unit-cost tradeoffs in the console.
[05:16] Tara (Infra): audit / logging — we need token-level cost and per-route latency traces forwarded to our observability. does your console expose that?
[05:25] Samir (SE): yes the Redwood Console gives per-route latency, token counts, and tracing hooks; you can export logs to Splunk or BigQuery. we'll include sample dashboards.
[05:35] Priya (CTO): security checklist: SOC2, ISO, SSO, KMS, data residency. can you confirm data retention policies for hosted POC?
[05:44] Alex (AE): for hosted POC you can opt-in to no retention or short retention windows; enterprise Private deployments give you full control. we'll include the retention options in the security pack.
[05:55] Ellen (Product): acceptance tests — can we codify them now? p95 < 700ms, extraction F1 > 0.95, no more than 5% invocation errors, and cost per 1k tokens under our target.
[06:08] Jules (Solutions Eng): yep we'll draft an acceptance matrix and attach to the trial run.
[06:13] Marco (ML): benchmarks — will Redwood run multi-tenant load tests or do we run them from our infra?
[06:20] Samir (SE): we'll run jointly. Redwood SE will orchestrate the load harness against the trial endpoint while your infra team monitors VPC peering and network egress. we usually do two runs: baseline and peak stress.
[06:33] Tara (Infra): network — what ports, IPs, and egress should we expect?
[06:38] Samir (SE): we'll send a network allowlist doc with IP ranges and ports; for VPC peering there's a short config guide.
[06:45] Priya (CTO): if the POC shows promising results, what's the path to production? Dedicated reserved capacity or Private?
[06:52] Alex (AE): depends on your compliance needs and throughput. many customers start with Dedicated for predictable throughput, then move to Private for stricter residency. we can propose both options in the commercial deck.
[07:02] Ellen (Product): pricing — can we get a ballpark for Dedicated vs hosted for our token profile?
[07:07] Alex (AE): yes we'll send a tailored pricing sheet after we have the exact token estimates — that'll be part of the follow-up.
[07:14] Marco (ML): integration specifics: we want SDK examples for streaming + function calling + structured output enforcement. also a mapping doc if any parameter names differ.
[07:24] Samir (SE): we'll include Python / Node snippets, streaming examples, and a mapping guide. also a small sample project to drop into your repo.
[07:33] Jules (Solutions Eng): on structured outputs, to avoid hallucination and schema drift we'll use a combination of function schemas, constrained prompts, and automated post-validate with a small retry heuristic. we'll provide the validation library as part of the POC.
[07:48] Priya (CTO): one more — data masking for PII before sending to the model? can Redwood do client-side pre-processing hooks?
[07:56] Samir (SE): Redwood doesn't mutate your data; we provide SDK hooks so you can pre-process or mask locally. for Private deployments we can place additional middleware if desired.
[08:07] Tara (Infra): ops contact — who will be our SE point during the benchmark?
[08:10] Alex (AE): Samir will be lead SE; Jules will help with integration snippets, and I'll coordinate commercial and next-steps.
[08:18] Alex (AE): recap of next steps: send security pack, provision trial endpoint and keys, Verdant to send sample dataset, schedule benchmark run.
[08:27] Priya (CTO): sounds good. any blockers? not from our side if we get the docs and trial keys quickly.
[08:34] Alex (AE): great. we'll aim to have the security docs and trial keys out by Monday. thanks everyone.

End of call.
